style: Painterly sci-fi folk illustration: gouache and watercolor washes over crisp fine ink linework, 1980s science-fiction paperback cover, Moebius / Jean Giraud ligne-claire feel, warm ochre-orange-terracotta desert palette against cerulean or deep-indigo skies, wide 3:2 cinematic composition, no text, no lettering, no logos.
world: Kira, the small barren desert moon of the planet Lamina: bare orange-ochre sand and rock, wind-carved sandstone spires, mesas and needle-like pinnacles, thin dry air, sparse scrub. In the sky hangs Lamina, the home planet of all seven species: a huge living world, full, blue and round, with white cloud swirls, deep blue oceans and green-and-brown continents, filling a large part of the sky (never a gas giant, no rings, no bands, no second moon); by day the sky is a pale cerulean with thin streaky clouds, at night a deep indigo starfield with Lamina glowing blue-white. The colony is a small village of a few hundred souls: clustered rounded adobe domes and beehive towers of sun-baked plaster in sand, ochre, terracotta and faded blue, with round porthole windows, arched doorways, stairs cut into rock, tall slender antenna masts and mushroom-capped water/radio towers, cylindrical tanks and pipes of weathered metal, canvas awnings, earthen paths between buildings; at night the windows and doorways glow warm amber. Interiors are cozy cave-like domed rooms with round windows, hanging brass lanterns, woven rugs in red, orange and blue, clay pots and handmade objects. The inhabitants are seven alien species (Jomkar, Klast, Frem, Ripi, Lokweel, Srol, Tayran) living together in simple robes, tunics and work clothes; no humans.

chapters.title: Siboot
chapters.scene: Inside a cramped, dim colony shuttle, a young Ripi colonist, Siboot (sleek black cat-like alien in a simple travel tunic), presses close to a round porthole, gazing out at the barren orange-grey moon Kira hanging in black space, with the giant banded planet Lamina looming behind it. Cool starlight falls across his thoughtful, slightly foreboding face; a green jackal-like Frem with huge ears waits patiently behind him for a turn at the window.
chapters.place: colony shuttle in orbit above Kira

chapters.title: Armageddonette
chapters.scene: Night on Kira: a small cluster of colonists of several species stands frozen on a rocky rise at the edge of the domed village, staring up at the enormous banded face of Lamina. Across its night side, tiny sharp pinpricks of white-orange light bloom and fade like distant sparks. Their silhouettes are dark against the starry indigo sky; the mood is silent dread.
chapters.place: ridge at the edge of the colony, night

chapters.title: Governor Grad
chapters.scene: Dawn in the dusty main courtyard of the colony: a small, frightened but determined ring of colonists of all seven species stands around a flagpole where a plain white sheet has just been raised as a flag of peace. A sleek black cat-like Ripi, Siboot, stands at the center with one hand raised, calling out; others peer warily from doorways and around dome corners. Low golden sunrise light rakes across the sand, with Lamina pale in the morning sky.
chapters.place: main courtyard of the colony at sunrise

chapters.title: A Walk in the Garden
chapters.scene: At the end of neat rows of tomatoes and cabbages, the only green patch in the colony, Siboot (sleek black cat-like Ripi) holds up a small notepad while his companion Iburical stares in astonishment at a bare orange sand hill beyond the garden. Floating in the air above the hill is a faint, glowing, translucent idea-image of a perfect ice-cream sundae in a pure dish, like a shimmering thought made visible. Warm late-afternoon light, Lamina huge in the blue sky.
chapters.place: colony vegetable garden at the desert edge

chapters.title: Funeral for a Civilization
chapters.scene: In the crowded, lamp-lit colony cafeteria, Siboot (sleek black cat-like Ripi) stands at a simple rostrum with eyes closed in deep concentration; before him rows of colonists of all seven species sit with eyes closed and small headphones on. Above the crowd floats a single radiant glowing glyph of pure light, the first word of the mind-language eeyal, rippling outward like a soft wave. Tear-streaked faces, solemn amber light, a sense of grief turning into wonder.

chapters.title: Stargazing
chapters.scene: Night in a small domed observatory on the colony's edge: two colonists, Hortz and Fredegund, crowd around an old brass refracting telescope aimed through the open dome slit at the gigantic glowing planet Lamina. Fredegund sits at the eyepiece while Hortz leans eagerly over her shoulder, both electrified by a sudden discovery. Soft blue night light from the slit, a dim red work lamp, scattered star charts.

chapters.title: Siboot's Last Sermon
chapters.scene: Evening in the colony courtyard: an old, frail Siboot, a grey-whiskered black cat-like Ripi in a plain robe, stands at a small wooden lectern addressing a quiet crowd of colonists of all seven species, one hand raised as if saying farewell. A doctor at his side gently takes his arm to lead him away as he begins to falter. The huge banded planet Lamina rises behind the domes in fading golden light; the mood is tender and elegiac.

chapters.title: Shaleen's Sermon
chapters.scene: Blazing midday heat outside the small adobe radio shack with its tall antenna mast: Shaleen, a young crimson horse-like Lokweel woman with a curly purple mane, bursts through the door with tears of joy, gripping a startled fellow Lokweel by the shoulders and crying out toward the village. Inside the open doorway glow an old radio console and microphone; onlookers turn and run toward the shack. Harsh white sunlight, short shadows, Lamina pale in the hot sky.

chapters.title: Artigul the Teacher
chapters.scene: Night inside a small, lantern-lit adobe home: Artigul, the eeyal teacher, stands frozen mid-step as a dinner plate slips from his hands, eyes wide with sudden revelation. Around his head three distinct glowing aura-symbols orbit like small spirits, one cool and sharp, one warm and gentle, one golden and heroic, casting colored light on the walls; a hand-drawn list of names lies on the table. Through the round window, Lamina glows in the starry sky.

chapters.title: Sufupican's Inaugural Sermon
chapters.scene: Inside the radio shack, Sufupican, the new Third Shepherd of Kira, a female Tayran with a white skeletal beak-like skull, a single red eye and a dignified dark robe, sits before a battery of old knobs, dials and glowing tubes, leaning toward the microphone as she throws the transmit switch. The Jomkar technician Sertgrid, shaggy tan fur and horns, watches from beside the console. Warm instrument glow; through the window the enormous banded Lamina, where a billion listeners wait.

chapters.title: Mind Combat
chapters.scene: Feslym, a male Klast (pink-violet skin with blue marbling, a crest and a yellow duck bill), lies on a mat in his dark hut, palms up, eyes closed in aura-sleep. Above him the scene opens into a vast black dreamspace, the Land of Auras, dotted with tiny firefly lights, where two huge blazing spirit-orbs collide in a burst of interlocking glowing aura symbols, one cold violet, one fiery gold. Mystic, dreamlike, intense but bloodless.
chapters.place: Feslym's hut and the dream-space of the Land of Auras

chapters.title: Feslym's Daughter
chapters.scene: In the colony courtyard, the little Klast girl Kendra, pink-violet with blue marbling, a small crest and a yellow duck bill, stands as the darling of the village, delighted, receiving gifts: a farmer offers the season's first fruits, an old mother holds out hand-sewn clothes, a machine-shop worker presents a toy made of scrap metal. Her proud father Feslym, an adult Klast, watches warmly behind her. Bright, warm morning light, colorful and affectionate.

chapters.title: Gardbore
chapters.scene: Alone at night in the shuttered colony archive, Gardbore, a green jackal-like Frem with huge ears and a tubular snout, stands with eyes closed, his elegant hands raised and dancing gracefully through the air as if conducting an invisible orchestra, tracing the shape of the music. An old music machine glows on a shelf among stacked books, tapes and film reels; faint ribbons of light seem to follow his fingers. Warm lantern light, intimate and secret.

chapters.title: Sirk the Til
chapters.scene: A young Tayran boy, Skordokott, small and gangly with a white skeletal beak-skull and a red eye, walks along a sandy path among the dunes outside the colony with his pet Til, Sirk, a small sleek furry hunter with big ears and bright eyes, peeking happily out of his backpack. The boy is talking softly to his friend over his shoulder. Golden late-afternoon light, long shadows, Lamina large in the sky; gentle and tender.

chapters.title: Zubi and Locksher
chapters.scene: At a remote desert pumphouse of weathered pipes and tanks, Locksher, a crimson horse-like Lokweel with a curly purple mane, stands drenched at the center of a huge fountain of water spraying out between his fingers from a burst valve. Zubi, a young Srol woman with a bright blue bald dome head, has collapsed on the sand nearby, helpless with laughter. Sparkling spray against the cerulean sky, rainbows in the mist, comic and warm.

chapters.title: Wiki and Skordokott
chapters.scene: In the colony cafeteria at mealtime, the stern old Lokweel cook Tekula, crimson with a grey curly mane and an apron, upends a pail of kitchen scraps onto the head of the tall, powerful Tayran Skordokott (white skeletal beak-skull, red eye), who blinks in total confusion. Diners edge away; in the background, the black cat-like Ripi Wiki leans against a doorway with a sly, mischievous grin. Warm interior light, comic.

chapters.title: Vetvel at Work
chapters.scene: At the irrigated fields at the edge of the colony, Vetvel, a female Jomkar with shaggy tan fur, horns and octagonal goggle eyes, lounges in the shade of an open equipment shed. Locksher, the crimson horse-like Lokweel crew chief, leads his dusty, tired crew in off their shift and chats with her, while the tall Tayran crew chief Skordokott drives his workers among the green crop rows and irrigation pipes behind. Bright hot afternoon, dust in the air.

chapters.title: Illness
chapters.scene: A dim adobe bedroom lit by a single lantern: the old Shepherd Feslym, a frail aging Klast (faded pink-violet skin, crest, yellow bill), lies propped in bed, smiling weakly at Vetvel, the shaggy tan horned Jomkar with octagonal goggle eyes, who bends close to hear him. His wife Nafimko, also a Klast, and a doctor stand by gravely; in the doorway behind, Kendra, his grown daughter, pauses, bracing herself. Quiet, somber, tender.

chapters.title: The Judge of the Campaign
chapters.scene: Evening in the busy colony cafeteria: at the entrance, Flanl, a prim elderly teacher, lectures Vetvel (shaggy tan horned Jomkar with octagonal goggle eyes) with a raised finger, while at a nearby table Zubi, the bright-blue bald-domed Srol, smirks into her cup. Across the room the black cat-like Ripi Wiki waves Vetvel over with a jaunty grin. Warm lamplight, chatter, a subtle undertone of rivalry before the campaign.

chapters.title: Eyes
chapters.scene: Around the deathbed of the old Klast Shepherd Feslym, whose eyes have just closed, the seven acolytes stand in a tight ring in a dim lantern-lit room: the Jomkar Vetvel, the Klast Kendra, the Frem Gardbore, the Ripi Wiki, the Lokweel Locksher, the Srol Zubi and the Tayran Skordokott. Grief on their faces is already giving way to wary sidelong glances as they size each other up. Dramatic chiaroscuro, faces lit from below, the shadow of Lamina in the window.
chapters.place: Feslym's bedroom at the moment of his death
